title: The half-filled optical Su-Schrieffer-Heeger-Hubbard model with uniaxial strain
authors: Jonah Huang, James Neuhaus, Benjamin Cohen-Stead, Steven Johnston, Richard Scalettar
abstract: Strain offers a direct route to control electronic phases by altering bond lengths, hopping amplitudes, and lattice symmetries. These aspects make electron-phonon (e-ph) coupled systems a natural setting to study strain-induced effects. The Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) Hamiltonian describes the coupling between itinerant electrons and lattice degrees of freedom that modulate hopping and is thus expected to be strongly affected by strain fields. At half-filling and on a bipartite lattice, the SSH interactions drive dominant bond-order-wave (BOW) correlations at low- temperature in which short bonds with high kinetic energy alternate with long bonds with low kinetic energy along four possible patterns. We model uniaxial strain through anisotropic hopping, which breaks the $90^\circ$ rotational symmetry and reduces the BOW phase degeneracy to two. We also include an on-site Hubbard U that promotes antiferromagnetic correlations that are also (weakly) driven by the SSH interaction itself. We map out the half-filled phase diagram in the plane of the e-ph and Hubbard couplings, and determine the critical temperature of BOW formation. Using analytic continuation, we also evaluate the spectral function and demonstrate directionally dependent gap formation in the BOW phase
summary: This work models the half-filled SSH-Hubbard system under uniaxial strain to study the competition between Bond-Order-Wave (BOW) and Antiferromagnetic (AFM) phases. Using advanced Quantum Monte Carlo simulations, the authors map the phase diagram and demonstrate that strain significantly influences the stability and characteristics of the resulting electronic order. This provides theoretical insight into strain-tunable correlated electronic phases.
main_problem: The study investigates the interplay between Bond-Order-Wave (BOW) correlations and Antiferromagnetic (AFM) correlations in the half-filled SSH-Hubbard model when subjected to uniaxial strain.
main_result: Uniaxial strain anisotropically modifies the phase diagram, shifting the competition toward the BOW phase and allowing for the quantification of the BOW transition temperature.
method: The research employs Determinant Quantum Monte Carlo (DQMC) simulations combined with Hybrid Monte Carlo (HMC) updates for phonon fields, and uses analytic continuation to analyze spectral properties.
model_or_system: The system is the optical Su-Schrieffer-Heeger-Hubbard (SSHH) model on a 2D square lattice, incorporating electron-phonon coupling ($\lambda$) and on-site Hubbard repulsion ($U$). Strain is modeled via anisotropic hopping, breaking rotational symmetry.
key_observables: Equilibrium phase diagram (BOW vs. AFM), spectral function showing directionally dependent gap formation, and correlation functions for both BOW and AFM order.
important_parameters: Half-filling ($ho=1$), dimensionless e-ph coupling ($\lambda$), Hubbard coupling ($U$), and the strain parameter ($\delta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis uses the leading-order expression for electron-phonon coupling and relies on the DQMC method being applicable due to particle-hole symmetry at half-filling.
figures_summary: The phase diagram maps the competition between AFM and BOW order in the $(\lambda, U)$ plane, showing how strain shifts the boundaries.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the SSH-Hubbard model with strain, details the DQMC/HMC simulation methodology, maps the phase diagram by varying $\lambda$ and $U$, and finally analyzes spectral properties in the ordered phases.
why_interesting: The combination of electron-phonon coupling, strong correlations (Hubbard $U$), and external tuning (strain) makes this highly relevant for understanding emergent electronic phases in correlated materials.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Correlation ratios for the (a) BOW and (b) AFM phases for δ = 0.3t, U = 5t, and Ω0 = 0.5t. The critical value of the dimensionless coupling λc in the thermodynamic limit is obtained from the intersection of the interpolated curves for the different lattice sizes L = βt = 8, 10, 12, as indicated by the dashed lines.

FIG. 3. Local observables as a function of the e-ph coupling strength for fixed δ = 0.3t, U = 2t, and Ω0 = 0.5t. Results are shown for the average values of (a) the double occupancy D; (b) the root mean square displacements Xrms and Yrms; (c) the direction-resolved kinetic energies Kx and Ky, and the AFM susceptibility χAFM. Results are also shown for different lattice sizes L as indicated by the legend in panel (a). Here, we find that the L dependence is weak, as is often the case for local observables. Panel (d) shows an additional global observable– the AFM susceptibility, χAFM.

FIG. 2. Ground state phase diagram of the optical SSHH model at half-filling in the plane of e-ph coupling and on-site repulsion U. Here phonon frequency Ω0 = 0.5t and strain δ = 0.3t. Blue open triangles give the BOW phase boundaries and red open triangles give the AFM phase boundaries. We show results for the unstrained case, δ = 0, (from [58]) for comparison (filled symbols). The shaded regions indicate coexistence. Figures 1 and 3 were obtained using data from the line cuts at U = 5t (green dashed line) and U = 2t (yellow dashed line), respectively.

FIG. 4. Crossing of the rescaled structure factors for the BOW phases for U = 4t, Ω0 = t, and λ = 1 for the strained δ = 0.3t case. We use the exponent ratio γ/ν = 7/4, which is shared by the Ashkin-Teller, four-state-Potts, and Ising universality classes in 2D.
